Definition: perhaps from σίνομαι (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant):--mustard.
BiblicalUsage: Sinapi is the mustard seed, the smallest seed in the garden, and Jesus uses it twice for the kingdom and twice for faith. The kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed that grows into a tree where the birds lodge, and faith as a grain of mustard seed can say to a mountain, remove hence, and it shall remove.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe smallness is no objection to God. A mustard seed is nothing in the hand and a tree in the garden, and I hold that faith the size of it is enough for mountains.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Mustard Seed
